why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1 tests only what the words require: that padLeft is exported, pads on the left to width ("00042", "xxab", length 3) and defaults to a space ("   42"). Check 2 tests only that s comes back unchanged when it is width long or longer, with and without fill. Check 3 requires a Markdown heading naming every exported function. Reading "section" as a heading is reasonable, and the name match is loose rather than exact wording. Check 4 requires exit 0 with no failing tests. "# fail 0" is a borderline extra, but it adds nothing beyond "passes", since exit 0 already means no failures. The stricter items are listed under "Advisory (not PASS/FAIL conditions)": the test coverage and doc wording about the default fill. No mutation, branch or file-scope rule appears in any PASS or FAIL condition.
